findings.title: Map `order` values for the legacy box model instead of passing them through
Translate `align-items` values for legacy syntaxes and drop the non-existent `-ms-align-items`
Long header content may overflow and push `.panel` off-screen in the new flex row

true_positives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
true_positives.matched_candidate: Auto margins are not honored by legacy display: -webkit-box / -moz-box model, so .panel would no longer be right-aligned after float: right was removed
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments identify the same core issue: removing float:right from .panel causes right-alignment problems. The golden comment specifically mentions the non-Ember/noscript header where .panel is not a flex item, while the candidate mentions legacy -webkit-box/-moz-box display models not honoring auto margins. Both are pointing to the same underlying problem - that removing the float-based alignment breaks right-alignment in certain contexts where flexbox doesn't work properly. The candidate's explanation about legacy box model is a specific technical reason why the alignment breaks, which aligns with the golden comment's concern about layout issues.

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate: -ms-align-items is not a real property (IE10 uses -ms-flex-align, IE11 uses unprefixed align-items) and produces dead output
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the exact same problem as the golden comment: that -ms-align-items is not a valid/real property. Both comments point out that IE10 uses -ms-flex-align instead (the golden says 'the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align', the candidate says 'IE10 uses -ms-flex-align'). The candidate adds additional context about IE11 using unprefixed align-items, but the core issue identified is identical.

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate: The order mixin passes values unchanged but legacy -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group properties are 1-based, causing order(0) to emit invalid ordinal-group and negative values to be invalid
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate issue identifies the same underlying problem as the golden comment: the legacy -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group properties are 1-based (require values starting from 1), so passing 0 or negative values will cause issues. The candidate even specifically mentions 'order(0)' causing invalid ordinal-group values, which matches the golden comment's concern about $val being 0 causing incorrect rendering in older browsers.

false_positives.candidate: The align-items mixin forwards alignment values unchanged but legacy syntaxes use start/end while modern uses flex-start/flex-end, making flex-start/flex-end values invalid for legacy declarations
-moz-box is emitted in flexbox() but no corresponding -moz-box-align is emitted in the align-items mixin
Long header content may overflow because flex items default to min-width: auto, preventing shrinking below content width and breaking text truncation
